data.text: Good, I can see the structure. Now let me run a query to get the top 3 states by average order value in 2018 with at least 500 orders.

args.purpose: Top 3 customer states by average order value in 2018 (with at least 500 orders)
args.sql:
WITH filtered_orders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, c.customer_state,
           SUM(oi.price) as revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) = 2018
    GROUP BY o.customer_id, c.customer_state
),
state_totals AS (
    SELECT customer_state,
           COUNT(*) as order_count,
           SUM(revenue) as total_revenue,
           AVG(revenue) as avg_order_value
    FROM filtered_orders
    GROUP BY customer_state
    HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500
)
SELECT customer_state, order_count, total_revenue, avg_order_value
FROM state_totals
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC
LIMIT 3
